mission_3.prediction: On the open map, both social settings produced complete preview paths that moved slightly farther away from the person than the baseline. On the constrained map, social_1 produced a complete path, while social_2 got stuck and oscillated near the person and wall. Social_2 used a higher repulsion strength and a larger influence distance, so I cannot tell from this comparison which change caused the oscillation.
mission_3.comparison: For A*, social_2 had the largest minimum person clearance at 0.841 m, compared with 0.725 m for the baseline. Time inside the 0.75 m personal-space threshold fell from 1.6 seconds to 0 seconds. The social_2 run took 46.90 seconds, compared with 46.54 seconds for the baseline, an increase of about 0.36 seconds. For RRT, the baseline had the largest minimum clearance at 1.742 m. Both social_1 and social_2 were slightly lower, at 1.731 m and 1.729 m. All three RRT conditions spent 0 seconds inside the personal-space threshold. In these runs, the baseline already left substantial space around the person, and neither social setting increased its measured minimum clearance.
mission_3.recommendation:
I would keep the RRT baseline for this scenario. It succeeded with a minimum person clearance of 1.742 m and took 43.83 simulated seconds. As an alternative, A* with social_2 also succeeded, but its minimum clearance was 0.841 m and it took 46.90 seconds. Both spent zero recorded seconds inside the 0.75 m threshold.

These results come from one trial per condition with a static simulated person. They cannot tell us how the robot would respond to someone walking
